title: Using AI chatbots in my game and getting charged for it
author: muilenta
selftext:
Okay, so I built my murder mystery game, and the NPCs are all chatbots that are sort of smartish.  They sometimes say stuff that is inconsistent with the game, but I feel like random and interesting things they say make up for it.  I do get charged like a dollar for like eight hours someone spends chatting with them.  Has anyone else been messing around with this type of game.  It's at [cityofsecrets.org](http://cityofsecrets.org) if you want to mess around with it.  I enabled the ability to generate images of what's going on in the interactions, but didn't enable that by default, because that could get expensive pretty quickly. 

https://preview.redd.it/qzdrjjc3je6h1.png?width=1288&format=png&auto=webp&s=1f40c7c21914b9b2da62d491907392881984c763

comments.author: EnumeratedArray
comments.body: Just make sure to add cost limits in case someone breaks something or decides to exploit a bug that ramps up your usage. Have a fallback so when a cost limit is reached the NPCs just fallback on static text.

replies.author: Coindk
replies.body: This, exploiters and bots are already looking at any security issue you could have leading them to use your resources freely while you will be charged for thousands of dollars with no way to do anything against it except pay.

replies.author: muilenta
replies.body: I set it up so that by IP only a certain amount to prompts can be requested, and then I set a budget in Azure so that I can't get decimated, but I've heard about people getting charged thousands of dollars in the past, so I'm always a little uncomfortable. I just feel like the smart NPC games are coming, and hoped to get in on it.

comments.author: PatchyWhiskers
comments.body: You need to figure out how to charge for this feature.

replies.author: muilenta
replies.body: I'm pretty clueless with charging.  I was thinking Patreon to try to make enough money back to at least cover the services.  The chat is pretty cheap, but when I allow the images to be generated, that gets expensive very quickly.

replies.author: Aware-Source6313
replies.body: Trying to make the costs with quantity of users/subscriptions is risky too because then your biggest fans who play the game the most will be your biggest costs and in a weird way you will be incentivized to reject your whales, which just doesn't seem like how you want to grow a fanbase as  a dev. Idk I don't think Patreon is a bad way to monetize but if your game can balloon in costs basically unbounded but your subs are a flat rate every month, you are taking a lot of risk

replies.author: monsterfurby
replies.body: The alternative would be to add bring-your-own-key for players who have an OpenRouter account anyhow.

replies.author: muilenta
replies.body: I saw something about this.  Thanks, I'm going to go see if I can figure this out.

comments.author: Gripppp
comments.body:
Very dangerous for your wallet
Do not just think from a token usage perspective. Think of all cases.

Someone can reverse engineer your game and use your AI as a backend for their end
Make sure to put a lot of guardrails on the AI itself. Consider cheap chinese models and lastly consider hosting your own LLM or embed it as part of the game build (will make the game explode in size)
But in general there very expensive lessons to be learned from this experiment

replies.author: muilenta
replies.body: I was thinking about using my own LLM.  They mentioned this at the Microsoft build conference, and I would be able to sleep better at night lol.

comments.author: Puzzleheaded-Way542
comments.body:
Enjoyed having a go, but it was hard to know what esch place in the city was, spent ages trying to find the hotel, and still didn't find the right one. You need a notepad or something so players can reference information to ask people about, I have the memory of a goldfish and I coudnt ever remember the room number.

There's positioning problems with characters on mobile and sometimes desktop, they float in the air etc.

Seems fun, good idea.

replies.author: muilenta
replies.body: Oh ya, I need to add a mobile splash screen that says the game was made for PC, or people are going to hunt me down, lol

comments.author: adpowah
comments.body: I feel like this is risky. Likely you could get this functionality in a smaller, preferably local package and eliminate the risks.

replies.author: muilenta
replies.body: If someone burns through the $300 Azure limit I set, it would not be the end of the world, but I just worry that Azure is going to come back with a $2000 bill and say I only set a bill for n feature, or something lame like that, heh.

comments.author: Calm_Look_3206
comments.body: What model? Look into deepseek. Decent quality for its cost.

replies.author: muilenta
replies.body: Seems like I tried that early on, and it worked pretty well.  Some of them censor when it doesn't make any sense, so I'm trying to get around that too.

comments.author: Aware-Source6313
comments.body:
Dude if your game got popular you would start burning cash. Usually the idea of a digital product is the cost doesn't increase when you scale it (minus server costs for multi player games/web apps, which scale reasonably into thousands of users). If you have a thousand players constantly it sounds like you are burning $125 per HOUR. You should bundle a tiny local llm with the game to run on the client's machine, and try to keep it accurate with strong context management. 

Honestly the thought that the murder might be unsolvable based on how the llm feels when giving answers doesn't appeal to me, usually mysteries are intricately crafted and little details can matter, if the details are made up on the fly I wonder how well it would work. Often the writing is a big part of mystery games. But if you think they add to the experience, bundling a small llm model with the game would be how I would approach it. I believe some others have already done it this way.

replies.author: muilenta
replies.body: If I can get to thousands of players, that would be a great problem to have.  I would probably start monetizing, and hopefully make more than they charge, heh.  As the game progresses, and the damsel in distress is getting ready to be sentenced to prison, the smart characters get smarted and start dropping more hints.   It is still possible to lose though.

comments.author: Vast_Emu_2346
comments.body: Have you considered making it a downloadable offline App that uses local LLM instead of an api? Seems way safer than using those big house ais

replies.author: muilenta
replies.body: I tried, but the LLMs that I tried were pretty terrible compared with what openai and anthropic or even xai offered.  I'm still pretty new to it through.
